problems.title: SASS vocabulary

options: integer compare that sets a predicate

hints: SASS mnemonics name type and space.
problems.solution: FFMA is FP32 FMA; LDG.E.128 a 16-byte vector global load; LDL/STL local memory (spills or arrays indexed dynamically); ISETP an integer compare writing a predicate register.

problems.title: Counting a loop
problems.statement: A hot loop's SASS, per iteration: 4 × LDG.E, 4 × FFMA, 2 × IMAD (address), 1 × IADD3, 1 × ISETP, 1 × BRA.
problems.solution: 13 instructions, 30.8% FMAs. Each FMA needs a fresh load: a memory-bound streaming loop, and the overhead is affordable.

problems.title: The innocent constant

options: F2F conversions to double, a DMUL, and a conversion back

problems.solution: The double literal promotes the expression to FP64: conversions plus a DMUL, at 1/32 or 1/64 rate on consumer GPUs. Write 0.5f. Grepping SASS for F2F and DMUL finds these.

problems.title: Vector loads in a GEMM

parts.prompt: If you see 16 × LDS instead of 4 × LDS.128…
options: the shared arrays aren't aligned or laid out for vector loads: issue count quadruples for loads

problems.solution: 4 vector shared loads feeding 64 FFMAs. 16 scalar loads would drop the FMA share from 94% to 80%. The SASS shows instantly whether vectorisation happened.

problems.title: Reading -Xptxas -v
problems.statement: ptxas info: Used 128 registers, 24 bytes spill stores, 24 bytes spill loads.

parts.prompt: Matters most if the spills are…

problems.solution: 6 values. Spills outside loops are harmless; inside the k-loop each becomes an L1 round trip per iteration. Check where the LDL/STL instructions sit in the SASS.

problems.title: Recovering the unroll factor
problems.statement: A loop over k = 0..255 shows, per iteration of the SASS loop, 32 FFMA, 2 LDS.128 and 1 BRA. Each source iteration does 4 FMAs.
problems.solution: Unrolled 8×: 32 SASS iterations of 32 FFMAs each. The branch now costs 1 instruction per 32 FMAs.

problems.title: Virtual versus physical

options: Virtual registers are SSA-style names; values not live at the same time share physical registers

problems.solution: PTX creates a new name for nearly every value; allocation maps them onto as many physical registers as are simultaneously live (Chapter 6.3).

problems.title: Predicated exit
problems.statement: @P0 EXIT at the top of a kernel.

options: exit the kernel for lanes where P0 is true

hints: Predicates turn instructions off per lane.
problems.solution: The bounds check if (i >= n) return; compiled to a predicated exit: no branch at all.

problems.title: Red flags

options: F2F or DMUL in an FP32 kernel

problems.solution: Spills, accidental FP64 and per-element 64-bit address arithmetic are red flags; FFMA-heavy code and vector loads are what you want.

problems.title: PTX versus SASS for performance work

parts.prompt: To check whether registers spilled and how loads were scheduled, read…
To check whether the front end unrolled a loop or contracted an FMA, PTX is…

problems.solution: Allocation, spills and final scheduling only exist in SASS. High-level decisions (unrolling, contraction, vector types) are already visible in PTX, which is easier to read.
